comments.body:
Implemented on branch `rad-sprint1` (7 commits) + `tree-sitter-rad` main (2 commits).

Grammar: `shell_stmt` is dissolved. `$` takes only a primary and `shell_cmd` is an ordinary `primary_expr`, so `$cmd` is an expr_stmt and `x = $cmd` an assign - capture targets, `catch:` blocks and precedence come from rules that already define them. Accessors are plain `.name` postfix validated by the checker, not new grammar (making `.stdout` a literal would keyword-extract `stdout`, which is the canonical capture target name). Generated with zero new conflicts.

Found while checking whether it could parse: a third silent footgun the card didn't know about. ``$`cmd` catch "x"`` and ``$`cmd` ?? "x"`` bound the handler to the *command string*, so it never ran and the failure killed the script - and `rad check` said nothing. That is now the lead of the migration guide.

Card's Edges, all closed:

- Spawn failure on `$list` was worse than described: an uncatchable RAD20042 internal bug with a Go stack trace, not just a missing code. Now 127/126, catchable, with `TestParams.RealShell()` added so the real executor is testable at all (it had no coverage).
- tree-sitter-rad, `rad fmt`, checker diagnostics, docs: done. Highlighting needed nothing - the tmLanguage grammar matches a bare `$` by regex.
- `rad fmt` turned up a pre-existing bug: statements with a trailing `catch:` block had the block dropped, so fmt declined the whole file. Latent because shell was the common carrier of `catch:` and used to be emitted verbatim.

Not blessed, as agreed: ``$`cmd`.ok`` as a bare statement works and is undocumented.

Evidence the statement form is untouched: of 7 syntax-tree snapshots that moved, every AST is byte-identical - only parse trees changed. One exception, a span that grew to cover parens that used to belong to lambda body syntax.

RED-10 written (Implemented). Migration guide, error docs RAD40025/40026/20048, SYNTAX.md, both guides.

BLOCKED ON YOU: go.mod still carries a local `replace` for tree-sitter-rad, uncommitted per AGENTS.md. Tag the grammar v0.10.0 and bump the dep to make the branch build standalone.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From the 2026-08-13 design session on the "ONE LAST TANGENT THOUGHT" in
`docs/thinking/shell_cmds.md` (2025-10-13 entry).

## Motivation

Consuming a command's output takes an assignment dance today, even when only
one value is wanted:

    stdout = $`git branch --show-current` catch:
        print_err("Failed to get branch")
        exit(1)
    branch = stdout.trim()

Query-style commands (`git status --porcelain`, `which x`, `git branch
--show-current`) are among the most common shell uses in real scripts, and
each costs a throwaway variable and extra lines. Shell invocations are
statements-only, so output can't feed an `if` or a function argument directly.

## Design: virtual accessors

A shell invocation becomes legal in expression position only when immediately
followed by one of four accessors: `.stdout`, `.stderr`, `.code`, `.ok`.
There is no result object type - the accessor is part of the invocation
syntax, and the four names match named-assignment vocabulary.

    branch = $`git branch --show-current`.stdout.trim() catch "unknown"

    if $`git status --porcelain`.stdout.trim():
        print_err("Uncommitted changes!")

    if not $`which docker`.ok:
        exit(1)

Settled semantics:

- **Capture follows the accessor**, exactly like named assignment: `.stdout`
  captures stdout and streams stderr; `.stderr` the reverse; `.code`/`.ok`
  capture nothing. So ``x = $`cmd`.stdout`` behaves identically to
  ``x = $`cmd` ``.
- **Stream accessors throw, status accessors don't.** `.stdout`/`.stderr`
  propagate on non-zero exit, composing with `??`/`catch`/`catch:` as usual.
  `.ok` (bool) and `.code` (int) never propagate - using them is the
  handling (grep's exit 1 is data, not failure). This deliberately differs
  from statement-form `code = $cmd`, which still propagates; the docs should
  own that asymmetry in a sentence.
- **No truthiness.** A bare invocation in expression position (``if $`cmd`:``)
  is a check-time error. Forcing `.ok` vs `.stdout` kills the shell ambiguity
  between "succeeded" and "printed something".
- **One value inline, several via assignment.** Expression form never yields
  both streams from one run; multi-capture assignment already covers that.
- **⚡️ echo stays on** in expression position - under `and`/`or`
  short-circuit it shows which commands actually ran. `quiet` and `confirm`
  remain prefix modifiers and work in expressions. Declining a `confirm`
  already synthesizes "exited 1 without running" (`core/shell.go:174`), so it
  composes with no new semantics.

## Grammar change and migration

Today `$` swallows a whole expression and postfix *builds the command*:
`$cmds[1]` and `$parts.join(" ")` both run today. New binding: `$` takes only
a primary (backtick/quoted literal, bare identifier, list literal, or
parenthesized expression); postfix after that refers to the *result* and must
start with an accessor. Computed commands move into parens - `$(cmds[1])` -
which already parses and runs today, so no new form is added.

Breaking, but loudly: old computed-postfix like `$cmds[1]` becomes a
check-time error with a fixit (`$(cmds[1])`). Zero silent reinterpretations:
accessor names on a command string already crash at runtime today. Related
gap to close while here: postfix currently binding to the command string is
itself a silent footgun - ``$`echo hi`.upper()`` runs `ECHO HI` and the
checker says nothing.

## Not blessed

``$`cmd`.ok`` as a bare statement (run, stream, never fail) falls out of the
grammar. Allowed, but do not document it as the idiom over `catch: pass` -
we expect a better, less cryptic syntax for that case later.

## Edges

- Spawn failure on the `$list` no-shell form (binary missing, not
  executable) must map to code 127 / `.ok == false`, or the status
  accessors' no-throw contract has a hidden crash path.
- tree-sitter-rad, highlighting, and `rad fmt` need the new binding.
- Checker: diagnostics for illegal postfix after an invocation, bare
  invocation in expression position, and the migration fixit.
- Docs: guide/shell-commands, guide/error-handling cross-ref,
  reference/syntax.
title: Allow shell invocations in expressions via result accessors
